narrative: The model estimated an 88.2% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That high estimate is why your law school application was denied: the decision reflects a strong predicted risk of bar failure, not a judgment that you have already failed. The most influential factor was your third-year class standing, which was far from the accepted-student average (a third-year decile of 1 versus about 5.8) and pushed the prediction toward failure. The second factor was your undergraduate GPA of 3.50, which is above the accepted-student average of 3.23 and therefore pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the academic-standing concerns. The third factor was your first-year class standing, which also differed sharply from the accepted-student average (2 versus about 6) and again pushed toward failure. To move forward, ask admissions for individualized feedback, provide any context or upward trend in your record, and consider strengthening your application with evidence of bar-readiness, additional academic coursework, or a revised study plan; discuss with an advisor whether retaking the LSAT or reapplying after improving your credentials would make sense.
